description: Connecticut data answers to the questions its news cycle is already asking. Every number fetched, never written.

items.content_text: The median unemployed US worker has been out of work 11.5 weeks (2026-09) — highest since May 2026. Source: PBS NewsHour (fixture) — Job growth cools as unemployment edges up in several states
items.title: When Americans lose a job, how long are they out?

items.content_text: Employers hired 3.3% of America's workforce into new jobs in 2026-08 — lowest since July 2026. Source: jobs-report fixture — Hiring slowed, layoffs are rare and hardly anyone is quitting: the labor market has frozen over
items.title: Is America still hiring people into new jobs?

items.content_text: Only 1.9% of US workers quit their jobs in 2026-08 — lowest since July 2026. Source: jobs-report fixture — Hiring slowed, layoffs are rare and hardly anyone is quitting: the labor market has frozen over
items.title: Are workers still confident enough to quit?

items.content_text: US layoffs and discharges ran at 1.0% in 2026-08 — lowest since April 2026 for this series, which began in 2000. Source: jobs-report fixture — Hiring slowed, layoffs are rare and hardly anyone is quitting: the labor market has frozen over
items.title: Are employers laying everyone off, really?

items.content_text: Labor's share of US nonfarm output sits at 93.4 on the 2017=100 index (2026-04) — lowest on record since the series began in 1947. Source: jobs-report fixture — Productivity gains keep rolling along while workers' paychecks fall behind
items.title: Are workers keeping their share of what they produce?

items.content_text: Connecticut's unemployment rate is 5.8% (2026), the 3rd-highest of 52 peers. Source: PBS NewsHour — Disappointing 29,000 jobs added in September as unemployment ticks up
items.title: Is Connecticut's job market doing better or worse than the rest of the country?

items.content_text: Bridgeport added $4.85B of net taxable property in 2025 (+59.9%), the fastest growth of 169 towns. Source: civic calendar — [civic calendar] 2026 general election (governor's race)
items.title: Which Connecticut towns grew their property tax base fastest?

items.content_text: 10.2% of Connecticut residents live below the poverty line (2024), the 15th-lowest of 52 peers. Source: civic calendar — [civic calendar] Fall safety-net and benefits enrollment coverage
items.title: How many Connecticut residents live below the poverty line compared with the rest of the country?

items.content_text: Connecticut reports 147 violent crimes per 100k people (2023), the 3rd-safest of 52 peers. Source: NYT U.S. (fixture) — California Couple Charged With Murder in Shooting of Son-in-Law
items.title: How safe is Connecticut compared with the rest of the country?

items.content_text: Connecticut's median gross rent was $1,550 in 2024, the 17th-highest of 52 peers. Source: NYT U.S. (fixture) — Renters battered by record shelter costs, national report finds
items.title: How expensive is renting in Connecticut compared to the rest of America?
